subject: chemistry
question_text: Give the equation that gives the relationship between ΔU and ΔH.

verification.note: Unit 6 Thermodynamics is sourced from the Sri Chaitanya Junior Fastrack chemistry section (book pp.73-75), which prints the question, its star rank and a model answer. Only ONE source book is held for chemistry — the TSBIE Basic Learning Material in hand covers physics only — so the two-book union check is PENDING a second chemistry source. This chapter has NO Long Answer section in the book, so no 8-mark form is invented. DISCREPANCY: the book defines Δn = nP − nR without restricting it to gaseous moles; this card writes the NCERT form, Δn(g) = gaseous product moles − gaseous reactant moles.

page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question

steps.label: The equation
lines: R = universal gas constant, T = temperature
steps.why: Enthalpy is H = U + pV, so ΔH differs from ΔU by Δ(pV). For ideal gases pV = nRT, and at constant temperature Δ(pV) = Δn(g)RT.
common_mistakes: Writing ΔU = ΔH + Δn(g)RT — the gas term adds to ΔU, giving ΔH.
Leaving the symbols unexplained. The meanings carry part of the mark.
steps.memory_tip: H carries the extra pV term, so ΔH equals ΔU plus the gas term Δn(g)RT.
steps.margin_note: The equation with symbol meanings earns this mark.

steps.label: What Δn(g) counts
lines: moles of gaseous products minus moles of
Solids and liquids are not counted.
steps.why: Only gases contribute a pV term of size nRT; the volume of solids and liquids is too small to matter. The source book writes Δn = nP − nR without the word gaseous — the gaseous restriction is the part the examiner checks.
common_mistakes: Counting solid or liquid moles in Δn(g).
Subtracting products from reactants instead of reactants from products.
steps.memory_tip: Only gas moles change the pV term. Count gases; ignore solids and liquids.
steps.margin_note: Say gaseous. Δn without the word gaseous is the common error.

insider_note: The mark that separates answers is the word gaseous in the meaning of Δn — the book's own answer omits it.
